He played [[college basketball]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina Gamecocks]]. ==Early life and high school career== Murray-Boyles was born on June 10, 2005{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Collin-Murray-Boyles/Summary/202374|publisher=[[RealGM]]|title=Collin Murray-Boyles}} and hails from [[Columbia, South Carolina]]. He attended [[A.C. Flora High School]] in [[Forest Acres, South Carolina]], where he was named the Class 4A Player of the Year as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] after helping Flora reach the state championship while averaging 34.3 points, 11.4 rebounds and 5.3 blocks.{{Cite web|url=https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/collin-murray-boyles-commits-to-south-carolina/101-8854985d-1bff-468e-a767-e4723f0be11f|publisher=[[WLTX]]|title=Collin Murray-Boyles commits to Gamecocks|date=August 7, 2022|author=Mack, Chandler}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-recruiting/article262695997.html|newspaper=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|url-access=subscription|title=Lamont Paris, Gamecocks offer hometown Class of 2023 forward |date=June 22, 2022|author=Bezjak, Lou}} He transferred to [[Wasatch Academy]] in [[Mount Pleasant, Utah ]], for his [[Senior (education)|senior]] season, and posted a team-leading average of 15 points and 8.8 rebounds per game; he was first in the conference in rebounds and third in points scored.{{Cite web|url=https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/ncaa/usc-gamecocks/gamecock-basketball/101-c873524d-153a-4bd9-8f67-37952037dbed|publisher=[[WLTX]]|title=South Carolina freshman, former A.C. Flora star is out indefinitely with mono|date=November 1, 2023|author=Anderson, Reggie}} ===Recruiting=== Murray-Boyles was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and a top-100 player nationally following his performance at Wasatch.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-state/142895472/|newspaper=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 31, 2023|page=B1, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-state/142895743/ B2]|author=Bezjak, Lou|title=Hometown star looks to make splash for Gamecocks}} All-Freshman Team.{{cite press release |url=https://www.secsports.com/news/2024/03/2024-sec-mens-basketball-awards-announced |title=2024 SEC Men's Basketball Awards announced |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 11, 2024 |access-date=March 11, 2024}} Following the conclusion of his sophomore season, he declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]] and received a green room invite in the second wave.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/45525667/six-more-players-receive-nba-draft-green-room-invites |title=Sources: Six more receive NBA green room invites }} ==Professional career== Murray-Boyles was chosen ninth overall in the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]]. On July 1, 2025, Murray-Boyles signed a rookie-scale contract with the Raptors.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-murray-boyles |title=Raptors Sign Murray-Boyles |date=July 1, 2025 | access-date=July 1, 2025}} On January 11, 2026, Murray-Boyles recorded 17 points, 15 rebounds, 3 blocks and 3 steals, propelling Toronto to a 116-115 overtime victory over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], becoming the first player in Raptors history to achieve those numbers in a game. {{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/fantasynews?Team=raptors#:~:text=unable%20to%20play.-,COLLIN%20MURRAY%2DBOYLES,ANOTHER%20IMPRESSIVE%20PERFORMANCE,-01/11/2026 |title=Another Impressive Performance |date=January 11, 2025| access-date=July 2, 2025}} On April 23, 2026, Murray-Boyles posted a playoff career high 22 points, along with 8 rebounds, in a 126-104 victory over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |last=Postrado |first=Jay |date=April 24, 2026 |title=Raptors upset Cavaliers, Collin Murray-Boyles secures Magic Johnson NBA Playoffs feat
